work.title: Pièces de clavecin qui peuvent se joüer sur le viollon

version.value: 2e Gigue of the Suite in D minor in Jacquet de La Guerre’s Pièces de clavecin qui peuvent se joüer sur le viollon (Paris, 1707), EJG.05, played with the first strain twice and the second strain once, without its repeat
version.note: The labels, the Internet Archive record, the BnF catalogue and the Oiseau-Lyre discography on medieval.org name only a Gigue and an Allemande; none names a book, suite or key, so the identification rests on comparing the recording with the printed scores. Pitch tracking of the transfer (mains hum removed; tuning 25 cents above A = 440, interquartile range 20–30 cents, as on the reverse side) finds an upbeat A5 at about 2.6 s; bar 1 from about 3.0 s with F5 in the right hand over left-hand D3, F3, A3 and D4; bar 2 over an E in the bass with C♯5, B♭4 and G4 above it; an E major harmony with G♯ at about 37.7–40 s, followed by an A major chord (A, C♯, E) at about 41–42.5 s; the same strain again from an upbeat A5 at about 42.7 s; a second strain from about 83.7 s that ends on a D minor chord at about 143 s; and no second pass of that strain. The first strain takes about 40 s and the second about 60 s. This agrees with the 2e Gigue of the D minor suite in the 1707 book (first edition, printed pages 13–14; Wiberg’s edition, printed pages 16–17): six-eight time, a right-hand upbeat A5, bar 1 on F5 over left-hand D, F, A and D, a first strain of 25 bars that reaches an E major chord with G♯ in bars 23–24 and closes on A major, and a second strain of 38 bars (27–64) that closes on D minor; at about 1.6 s a bar, 25 and 38 bars take about 40 s and 60 s. The earlier reading of the Gigue as centred on A minor, with a first strain ending on E with G♯, took the E major harmony before the A major chord of bar 25 for the close of the strain. Of the nine gigues and doubles in the two books, this is the only one in six-eight; the others are in 6/4 (1687: D minor, A minor, F major; 1707: D minor, its Double, G major), in 3/4 (1687, first G minor gigue) or in common time (1687, second G minor gigue). The file sounds a quarter of a semitone sharp, so there is no whole-tone offset that would turn a G minor or F major gigue into the recording. The earlier proposals, the F major gigue of 1687 (EJG.04) and the A minor gigue (EJG.03), could not be reproduced. The Allemande on the reverse comes from the other suite of the 1707 book, in G major, so the two sides of the disc are from different suites; no source states the pairing.

performers.note: The Bibliothèque nationale de France record reads “Isabelle Nef, clav.” and gives her dates as 1898–1976. The make of the instrument is not established.

date.note: The recording date is not stated in the sources consulted. The BnF record dates the disc 1942; an Oiseau-Lyre discography after Jim Davidson’s Lyrebird Rising (1994) gives its release as 1938 or 1939, recording site and date unknown (https://medieval.org/emfaq/cds/lol75.htm). The Internet Archive upload date of 25 October 2018 is not a session date.

place.note: No recording venue is established by the sources.

label.note: Named as publisher in the Internet Archive item. The label issued its first 78 rpm discs in December 1937.

catalogue.note: The Internet Archive description gives “Catalog number: O. L. 75”, and the label scan reads “O. L. 75” on both sides.

matrixTakeSides.value: PART 1296 (Gigue); the reverse side, the Allemande, is PART 1295

credits.note: The item’s description names an audio engineer at George Blood, L.P., and lists the item in the Boston Public Library and George Blood collections.

processing.value: Digitised at 78 rpm with four stylus sizes, flat and equalised; the engineer’s preferred version is the one offered, as a variable-bitrate MP3 derived from a 24-bit FLAC.
processing.note: The pitch of the file is about 25 cents above A = 440 (interquartile range 20–30 cents), as on the other side of the disc, and the identified score is in D minor, which sounds as written. The offset cannot be divided between the harpsichord’s tuning and the speed of the disc or its transfer; no speed correction was applied here.

digital.format: Internet Archive variable-bitrate MP3 derivative of a 24-bit FLAC transfer of one side of a 78 rpm disc

composition.value: Out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Jacquet de La Guerre died in 1729. This is a term calculation, not clearance of every edition.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis for a disc dated 1942 by the Bibliothèque nationale de France (release in 1938 or 1939 according to an Oiseau-Lyre discography), under the programme’s pre-1963 recording rule.
recording.note: The BnF date is a catalogue date for the disc, not an independently verified first-publication date; an Oiseau-Lyre discography (https://medieval.org/emfaq/cds/lol75.htm, after Davidson’s Lyrebird Rising) places the release in 1938 or 1939, and the label began issuing discs in December 1937. Either date is before 1963. The Gallica record marks its own digital copy as public domain; the Internet Archive item carries no licence. US first-publication evidence and US status are not established.
